reason: The mechanism verifies end-to-end and the quote is verbatim: ShopConfigLoader.java:260 defaults icon to Material.BARRIER, 289-293 keeps a MATERIAL entry with no icon.material (only a warning plus a loadWarnings entry that is summarized at 179-183), and the enclosing parseItem returns the item at 369 instead of null, so load() does not reject the entry; the shipped template is clean (only two MATERIAL entries, bow and arrow, both with icon.material at shop.yml:39-58), so the trigger is an admin-authored omission. ShopManager.deliverItem builds the product from the same field at ShopManager.java:135 (return new ItemStack(item.getIcon(), amount);), and ShopListener.purchase deducts at 126 before calling deliverItem at 135 with no material check, while the barrier path cannot reach either refund branch (BARRIER is a valid item, so no throw and product is non-null), so the player really pays and receives a barrier. Severity is nevertheless overstated: the GUI renders the same fallback (ShopGUI.java:73 new ItemStack(item.getIcon())), so the player sees a barrier block with its price before clicking rather than a bait-and-switch, and the loader emits both a per-item warning and an aggregated info line naming the id. It is also a deliberate, tested contract (comments at 282-288 explicitly accept the residual gap; ShopConfigMaterialValidationTest.java:44-93 and ShopConfigLoaderTest.java:415-437 pin 'keep the item, fall back to BARRIER'), taken to avoid silently losing a GUI slot, so the residual is a known admin-config edge case rather than an unnoticed high-severity defect; the stronger remedy would be to align it with the amount<=0 MATERIAL rule at 315-321, which skips the entry.
